title: Test published Nahuatl assignments with inflectional diagnostics
statement: I checked the authors' stated dialect criteria on pp. 74–77 against their illustrative assignments on pp. 72–73 and in the appendix (https://web.archive.org/web/20150226041323/http://cms.herbalgram.org/herbalgram/issue100/HG100-voynich-online.pdf). On f100r the authors assign nashtli through an illustrated cactus and compare it to nochtli, then use maguoey for an agave-like plant, which they identify as a loan via Spanish from Taino. Their other proposed forms include f99r tlacanoni for a paddle-shaped root, f102r (the authors’ notation) atlaan or atlan for a mineral illustration with droplets, and f100r choll-chi for an owl-like flower, which they analyze as partly Spanish. The examples therefore include comparison with an expected name, a descriptive name, alternate spellings and loan or mixed forms. Their use of tl as a dialect diagnostic mentions endings on p. 74, but the tl in tlacanoni is initial and nashtli ends in tli. They use chi as an ending and also analyze it in choll-chi as a lexical root. I found no geographically mapped sound correspondence for that root or diagnostic inflected paradigm among the examples motivating the dialect conclusion. As independent controls, Canger (2011), pp. 248–250, contrasts urban Tlatelolco/Tenochtitlan plural forms of 'go' with regional forms and contrasts urban perfect ki:s with Sierra de Puebla ki:sa-k for 'went out'. Canger also documents the diffusion of some urban innovations (p. 254). These comparisons require inflected forms from running text. The selected illustrative forms alone do not place the proposal in Morelos or Puebla or establish that its proposed dialect is extinct. Canger's open study is at https://nahuatl.historicas.unam.mx/index.php/ecn/article/download/26560/24897/51134.
check: Freeze a context-independent transcription and phoneme assignment from the published material before selecting running text. Predeclare multiple Nahuatl diagnostics, including plural forms of 'go' and stem-vowel retention across distinct perfect verb stems. Require connected passages with repeatable affix and stem correspondences. Compare against named colonial and modern varieties and report systematic matches, conflicts and missing evidence. Evaluate extinction separately with historical and speaker documentation once a variety is independently delimited.
